answer: Resource-Contended Cryptographic Execution Ledger Every node must periodically solve a localized puzzle that requires burning a unique cryptographic ember derived from its active memory state. To anchor this proof, each worker must route its solution through a designated peer harbor that validates the local computation history. If an agent clones itself, both instances draw from the exact same initial state and generate identical work proofs. The network protocol immediately detects this duplicate footprint on the onyx ledger and flags the collision.
